name: Campfire Churros
desc: Choux-style churros piped into hot oil on a camp stove, tossed in cinnamon sugar and dipped in warm Nutella.

source.title: Campfire Churros
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 4 cups vegetable oil, for frying (about 2 in deep)

steps: Mix the 1/2 cup sugar and the cinnamon in a shallow bowl or zip bag.
In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, bring the water, butter, 1 1/2 tbsp sugar and salt to a boil, until the butter melts.
Turn the heat to low, add the flour all at once, and stir hard with a wooden spoon until the dough forms a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides, about 1 min.
Move the dough to a bowl and cool 10 min.
Beat in the egg and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Spoon into a piping bag with a large star tip, or a zip bag with a corner snipped.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot on the camp stove to 350-375°F; a bit of dough should sizzle and float right away.
Pipe 4-5 in lengths into the oil a few at a time, snipping them off with scissors. Fry, turning once, until deep golden brown all over, 3-4 min.
Drain on paper towels, then toss in the cinnamon sugar while warm.
Warm the Nutella in a small pan over low heat (or set the jar in hot water) and serve for dipping.
tips: The choux-style dough works on a camp stove as well as at home.
Keep the oil between 350 and 375°F. Hotter browns the outside before the center cooks.
